request.spec:
A person may have a contact: a text on the person form, stored with surrounding spaces removed and
lower-cased, shown on the row. A contact already on the sheet (another person's) is refused with an
error on the form, and nothing is saved; a blank contact is none. PERSON_ADDED gains
contact=<contact> at the end when the form gave one; PERSON_EDITED gains contact=<contact> at the
end when the contact the form gave differs from the one stored (the empty value when it was
cleared).

agent.result_text:
I've added the person contact, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What it does now**
- The person form has a new contact field. A contact is saved with the spaces around it removed and in lower case, and a blank one counts as no contact.
- Each person's row shows their contact, or nothing when they have none.
- If another person on the sheet already has that contact (e.g. `CAM@X` when Cam has `cam@x`), the add or edit is refused with the form's error, and nothing is saved or written to the audit file.
- `PERSON_ADDED` ends with `contact=<contact>` when the form gave one. `PERSON_EDITED` ends with `contact=<contact>` only when the contact changed, and with `contact=` when it was cleared.

**What changed**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V51__person_contact.sql`, adds a `contact` column to the person table and to its history table, so past views of the sheet stay complete. It also adds a unique index on sheet and contact.
- **Server:** the contact is cleaned up in `ValidatePerson`, saved and loaded in `PersonStore`, and returned to the front end with each person. The duplicate check runs in `CheckNameFree` and `CheckNameFreeForEdit`, the same places that check for duplicate names, and refuses with a new `DuplicateContactException`. The two audit classes add the contact at the end of their lines. Quick-add still creates people with no contact.
- **Front end:** the form field (`person-form-contact`) and the row cell (`person-contact`), plus the new field on the `Person` type. I also updated the comments in the two person endpoint files to mention the contact.

One thing to know: if two people save the same contact at exactly the same moment, the database index stops the second one, but it would fail with a general server error instead of the normal form error. Only that race hits it; ordinary duplicates get the normal refusal.
